paper_title: Dynamic root microbiome sustains soybean productivity under unbalanced fertilization
access: Read full publisher HTML, results, discussion, figure captions, and methods including DNA spike-in timing, sampling design, and validation conditions. Original article open access CC BY 4.0.

verified_claims.claim: Four fertilizer treatments, including NPK control and omission of N, P, or K, were applied at a Harbin field experiment started in 1979; three plots per treatment; 2020 sampling at eight stages from days 1 to 72.
verified_claims.evidence_location: Methods: Experimental design, sampling, and measurement of soil chemical properties; Figure 1.

verified_claims.claim: Available P was 95% lower in the -P treatment; soybean yield was reduced by 25–29% in the two reported seasons. The -N treatment had no statistically significant yield difference from control, despite a 9% higher reported average.
verified_claims.evidence_location: Results: Effects of fertilization on soil chemical properties and soybean performance; Figure 1B–C.

verified_claims.claim: QMP used artificial DNA spike sequences during PCR amplification to estimate gene-copy abundances.
verified_claims.evidence_location: Methods: High-throughput sequencing and bioinformatic analysis. Spikes were mixed with extracted DNA before amplification, not added before DNA extraction.

verified_claims.claim: Actinobacteria relative abundance declined with plant age while absolute abundance rose by 2.1-fold in the rhizosphere and 18.8-fold in the endosphere.
verified_claims.evidence_location: Results: Assembly of root-associated microbiome during plant development; Figures 3–4.

verified_claims.claim: Under -P, rhizosphere bacterial load fell relative to control by 54%, 61%, and 75% at days 42, 60, and 72; the endosphere did not show the same consistent pattern.
verified_claims.evidence_location: Results: Assembly of root-associated microbiome during plant development; Figure 3B–C.

verified_claims.claim: SynCom5 increased dry weight at 2 weeks by 38% with added N and 18% without it relative to SynCtrl.
verified_claims.evidence_location: Results: A low-nitrogen-enriched cluster promotes plant growth; Figure 7E–F.

verified_claims.claim: Validation used sterilized vermiculite, nutrient solution with or without NH4NO3, 12 seedlings per treatment, inoculation after germination and one week later, and measurements at 2 and 3 weeks after first inoculation.
verified_claims.evidence_location: Methods: Rhizosphere microbial isolation and experimental validation.

verified_claims.claim: Nitrogen-fixation activity was not detected in any tested strain, although selected SynComs had greater IAA and ACC-deaminase measures and some strains solubilized inorganic phosphorus.
verified_claims.evidence_location: Results final paragraph before Discussion; Methods: Characterization of plant growth-promoting traits in synthetic communities.

limitations: One long-term field site and one detailed-sampling soybean variety; field soil legacy covaries with nutrient availability and other chemical differences.
No detected statistically significant -N yield benefit, and no proof that the selected SynCom alone caused field productivity.
Controlled SynCom growth tests measured young plants over weeks, not mature grain yield from field inoculation.
DNA marker copies do not directly equal viable cell counts or process rates.
Bradyrhizobiaceae-associated sequences were filtered from the endosphere 16S analysis to reduce effects of nodule symbiosis; rhizobia were additionally examined with rpoB.
Co-occurrence networks do not establish direct cooperation; functional-gene representation does not directly measure nutrient flux.
Sorghum does not normally form soybean-type nitrogen-fixing root nodules; transfer of outcomes needs crop-specific tests.
application_status: Temporal sampling, quantitative load measures, and process-based extensions to CPlantBox/DuMuX are proposed research ideas only. No software capability or validated sorghum parameter is claimed.
